subject.title: feat: audit PR review convergence at exact head

question: Should exact-head convergence become a supported OpenClaw repository script, or should this ClawSweeper-specific review-policy pilot live and evolve within the ClawSweeper-owned automation boundary?
rationale: The patch introduces a new automation contract and documentation surface rather than repairing an established runtime bug; repository policy identifies ClawSweeper review schemas and automation rules as owner-specific, so implementation placement and support commitment require maintainer intent.

options.title: Keep it in ClawSweeper
options.body: Move the pilot behind the ClawSweeper automation owner, where its verdict markers, proof policy, and follow-up lifecycle can share one supported contract.

options.title: Adopt a repository script
options.body: Explicitly support a generic repository-local audit, but first define its stable API, authoritative required-check source, and callers outside ClawSweeper.

options.title: Pause the pilot
options.body: Defer the new readiness mechanism until maintainers need it for a concrete merge workflow and can sponsor the API boundary.

recommendation.title: Keep it in ClawSweeper
recommendation.body: Move the pilot behind the ClawSweeper automation owner, where its verdict markers, proof policy, and follow-up lifecycle can share one supported contract.

likelyOwner.reason: fr-meyer authored the current proposal and is the only identifiable participant in the supplied PR history; a current-main automation owner needs maintainer identification.
